title: Montgomery's blues piano and Vivian from Kansas
summary: Little brother Montgomery left in Omaha to record in Chicago; a Kansas woman pianist named Vivian replaced him and came back to New Orleans with the band.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: But he left us in Omaha. He had to go make some records.

He had to go, some blues singer, a woman he knew in Chicago had sent for him to make some records. He was in Omaha. But he could stop or dance. That's right. That boy would get in one of them cab rats and get to play on that piano. He had one blues he would play. People would actually stop dancing and come stand around that piano. That's right. They would stop in the middle of the floor and just get to walk and see them one at a time, something like a moving picture. You see them just walking by that piano. And he'd sing that blues and play that piano. And after he went we picked up a woman from Attacan, Kansas. Her name was Vivian. I don't remember my last name but man, could she play some piano?

Gee. We missed Brada for the blues that she could play, but we never missed them when she was playing in the band. She could play. She came all the way down here with us and played with the band a while and after things started to slow it up she went on back. But she was very good. In Kansas, huh? Yeah, she's from Attacan, Kansas.
No, Attacan, Kansas. That's her home.
